world_news.headline: Australian politics live: Government lacks ‘moral authority’ on decarbonisation, Monique Ryan says; Labor MP kicked out of question time
world_news.summary:
• Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The government will save more than it spends, says Jim Chalmers, but it won’t be a “slash and burn” budget update.

Unlike the federal budget, where we get plenty of notice of when it will be handed down, the government only gives us a few days notice for the mid-financial year economic and fiscal outlook (or Myefo).

There’s still a fair bit of work to do to finalise it all, but we’ve made enough progress to be confident that at this stage there will be a modest net save in the budget.

We’re not going to slash and burn in the budget where that would impact the payments that people receive or where it would impact some of the more sensitive parts of the economy. But we haven’t focused the savings on just one portfolio. There will be a number of savings in the mid-year update. They will be substantial, as I said. These are serious times.

You can see in the quite extraordinary reaction on the stock market just how volatile global markets are right now. I think it’s a bit of a symbol of the quite extraordinary volatility, unpredictability that we’re seeing play out in markets in the AI sector, but more broadly as well.

world_news.headline: South Korea tells island residents to take shelter after Russian military aircraft approach
world_news.summary:
The order was issued after aircraft entered the country’s air defence identification zone over the island of Ulleungdo

Residents of a remote South Korean island were ordered to take shelter on Tuesday morning after several Russian military aircraft came close to entering its airspace, prompting a pre-emptive alert from the military that anticipated a violation.

The defence ministry said it would summon the Russian defence attaché on Tuesday afternoon to lodge a strong protest.

world_news.headline: Social media companies could be fined 5% of global revenue after Labor and Greens join forces on online safety laws
world_news.summary:
Individual Australians will be able to sue big tech firms for harm suffered online under compromise deal

  • Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Big tech companies may face “multibillion-dollar” fines and individuals could sue social media companies in court under Australia’s new digital duty of care laws, with the Greens to support the bill’s passage after extracting major amendments from Labor.

From late 2027, Australians will also be able opt out of addictive online algorithms under the new legislation, while the “endless scroll” of social media feeds may also cease.

world_news.headline: China sentences official to death for spying for foreign country
world_news.summary:
Accused official leaked national secrets to unnamed country and received payments worth over $150,000, state-linked publisher says

A Chinese official has been sentenced to death for spying for a foreign country, a government-linked publisher has said.

Gold Wall Press, a publishing company associated with China’s national administration of state secrets protection, said the convicted person was surnamed Ma and was approached and recruited by an unnamed foreign intelligence service while working abroad.
